source.section: Schedule 3 line 1 (PDF page 24: joint 2,000, all other filers 1,000), line 4 (PDF page 25: 1,000 age 65 or older), line 5 (PDF page 25: 500 age 65 or older and IT-40 line 1 under 40,000, or under 20,000 married filing separately); Schedule 2 line 11 code 632 and PDF page 22 Military Retirement Income and/or Survivor's Benefits Deduction; Schedule 2 lines 5 and 6 (PDF page 17 Lines 5 and 6: 'Indiana does not tax Social Security income or the railroad retirement benefits'); Form IT-40 lines 1-8 (PDF page 1; line 8 'multiply line 7 by 3% (.03)'); booklet PDF page 8 Line 1; PDF pages 5-6 rounding

worked: Federal AGI = military retirement person 0 30,000.00 + IRA distribution person 0 8,000.00 + taxable Social Security 16,400.00 = 54,400.00. Social Security received: person 0 20,000.00; the federal taxable amount from the federal worksheet is 16,400.00. Federal taxable income = 54,400.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 36,650.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored; Indiana starts from federal AGI). Form IT-40 line 1 federal AGI 54,400.00. Line 2 add-backs 0.00; line 3 = 54,400.00 + 0.00 = 54,400.00. Schedule 2: line 5 taxable Social Security 16,400.00; line 11 code 632 military retirement 30,000.00; line 12 total = 46,400.00. IT-40 line 4 = 46,400.00. Line 5 = 54,400.00 - 46,400.00 = 8,000.00. Schedule 3: line 1 1,000.00; line 4 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00; line 5 IT-40 line 1 54,400.00 is not less than 40,000.00: none; line 7 total = 2,000.00. IT-40 line 6 = 2,000.00. Line 7 = 8,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 6,000.00. Line 8 = 6,000.00 x 0.03 = 180.00. No credits; county tax (line 9) is local and out of scope. State income tax 180.00. The 500 test reads IT-40 line 1, before Schedule 2: line 5 is only 8,000.00 but federal AGI, which holds the military pension and taxable Social Security, is over 40,000, so the 500 is lost.
